Introduction
The adrenal medulla is considered a sympathetic ganglion (belonging to the sympathetic
nervous system) with endocrine evolution.
This concept is based on:
• The embryology of the adrenal medulla which is in favor of its neurological origin: the
adrenal medulla derives indeed from the neural crest (like the cells of the sympathetic
ganglia)
• Its histology which is in favor of a glandular tissue: indeed, the hormone-secreting cells
(chromaffin cells) are grouped in clusters around the capillaries.
• Finally, its neurophysiology: the three catecholamines are neurotransmitters synthesized by
the adrenal medulla and by nerve cells (splanchnic nerves).
o Adrenaline (epinephrine): accounts for 80% of the catecholamines stored in the chromafine
cells of the adrenal gland
o Noradrenaline (norepinephrine): stored mainly in the vesicles of the synapses of central and
peripheral noradrenergic neurons
o Dopamine: dopaminergic neurons are located primarily in the central nervous system

Role of bile acids contained in bile:
Bile acids come from the
catabolism of cholesterol in the
liver cell.
Cholesterol is first converted into
primary bile acids.
These primary bile acids when
combined with taurine and glycine,
give conjugated bile acids.
Conjugated bile acids pass through the common bile duct to the small intestine, where they
undergo the action of intestinal bacteria which transform them into secondary bile acids;
which are essential for the digestion of lipids. Subsequently, these bile acids can return to
the liver via the enterohepatic cycle if the body needs them, or be excreted in the stool.

excess iron is then excreted in the stools, thus preventing an increase in sideremia.
• Conversely, the reduction in circulating iron leads to a reduction in hepcidin and the
exit of cellular iron.

II- Specialized renal functional exploration
A- Glomerular filtration rate
1-Measurement of “Glomerular Filtration Rate” (GFR): Clearance
It assesses the ability of the kidney to filter plasma at physiological flow
Definition: The GFR of a glomerulus represents the volume of plasma crossing the
capillary wall of this glomerulus, per unit of time.
Concept of Clearance of a substance eliminated by the kidney:
Clearance = volume of blood purified of a substance, by the kidney, per unit of time.
If a substance is neither reabsorbed nor secreted, at the level of the tubule, its clearance is
